payload.question: Who will win the 2026 Rhode Island governor election?
payload.descriptionMarkdown:
This market resolves to the **candidate** who wins the 2026 election for **Governor of Rhode Island** — the term beginning in January 2027.

**Which round counts:** the November 3, 2026 general election (plurality winner). Primaries do not count.

**Answers:**
- **Helena Foulkes** — ballot designation: Democratic
- **Aaron Guckian** — ballot designation: Republican
- **Ken Block** — ballot designation: Independent
- **Another candidate** — any person other than the candidates listed above



**Party:** each candidate's party designation is shown for information only. This is a candidate market: a "No" on one candidate is a bet on any other winner, not on a particular party.

**Withdrawal, death or replacement:** the market resolves to the candidate certified as the winner. If a listed candidate is replaced on the ballot by someone not listed, and that person wins, it resolves to "Another candidate".

**Results:** resolves on the state's certified results. It may resolve earlier once the Associated Press has called the race and no recount, contest or runoff that could change the winner remains pending. If a recount or court-ordered correction changes the certified winner before resolution, the corrected certified result controls.

**Postponement or cancellation:** if the general election is postponed, the market stays open until the rescheduled election for the same term. If no election for this office and term is held, it resolves N/A.

Starting probabilities are seeds, not forecasts.

answerMeta.label: Helena Foulkes
answerMeta.partyEvidence: Won the Sep 9 2026 Democratic primary; inventory (RI certified list via Wikipedia)

seed.basis: SEED, not a forecast: reviewer-set from the post-primary poll cited on Wikipedia (Foulkes 44%, Block ≈25%, Guckian 17%), shaded for a plurality race with a 19-point lead; 2% to Another candidate (Gotra, Reynolds, write-ins).
seed.note: Initial pool probabilities only. Not an observed market forecast.

liquidityPlan.rationale: Competitive by seed (leader < 85%): tier 10,000 so a Ṁ100 trade moves the price by roughly a point, not ten.
liquidityPlan.alternatives: Lower: tier 1,000 everywhere. Higher: +extraLiquidity for marquee races. See dry-run report for price impact by tier.

evidence.whyCreate: audit decision needs-creation: No market can represent the leading independent (Ken Block).
evidence.snapshot: prod DB read-only 2026-10-03 00:50–00:58 UTC + name search of all 33,950 open markets
evidence.inventorySource: Wikipedia 2026 tables citing official certified lists (fetched 2026-10-03)

rejectedAlternatives.reason: Title-only R/D multi with no Other while independent Ken Block polls second; cannot represent his chance (addAnswers DISABLED).

payload.question: Which party will win the 2026 U.S. House election in Alabama's 1st District?
payload.descriptionMarkdown:
This market resolves to the **party** of the winner of the 2026 election for **U.S. Representative for Alabama's 1st congressional district** — the term beginning January 3, 2027.

**Which round counts:** the November 3, 2026 general election (plurality winner). Primaries do not count.

**Party rule:** the winner's party is the party **on whose line or with whose party designation they appear on the official general-election ballot**. A candidate nominated by Democratic Party or Republican Party who also appears on other parties' lines (fusion) counts as that party's candidate. Candidates who are independent, have no party preference, or belong to any other party resolve to "Another party or independent", even if they say they would caucus with a major party. Later party switches, caucus decisions, resignations or deaths after the result is certified do **not** change the resolution.

**Replacements:** if a nominee withdraws, dies or is replaced before the election, the market still resolves to the party of the certified winner; the names below are informational only.

**Results:** resolves on the state's certified results. It may resolve earlier once the Associated Press has called the race and no recount, contest or runoff that could change the winner remains pending. If a recount or court-ordered correction changes the certified winner before resolution, the corrected certified result controls.

**Postponement or cancellation:** if the general election is postponed, the market stays open until the rescheduled election for the same term. If no election for this office and term is held, it resolves N/A.

Candidates on the certified general-election list at the time of creation (October 2026, informational):
- Jerry Carl — Republican
- Clyde Jones Jr. — Democratic

Starting probabilities are seeds set mechanically from the district's partisan lean, not forecasts.

seed.basis: SEED, not a forecast: Cook PVI R+17, neutral national environment, logistic scale 4 pts → P(D|two-party)=1%, clamped to 3–97%; 2% reserved for another party/independent/write-in.

**Which round counts:** the November 3, 2026 general election if a candidate wins a majority of the votes; otherwise the December 1, 2026 runoff between the top two (O.C.G.A. 21-2-501). Primaries do not count.

**Party rule:** the winner's party is the party **on whose line or with whose party designation they appear on the official general-election ballot**. A candidate nominated by Democratic Party or Republican Party who also appears on other parties' lines (fusion) counts as that party's candidate. Candidates who are independent, have no party preference, or belong to any other party resolve to "Another party or independent", even if they say they would caucus with a major party. Later party switches, caucus decisions, resignations or deaths after the result is certified do **not** change the resolution.

**Replacements:** if a nominee withdraws, dies or is replaced before the election, the market still resolves to the party of the certified winner; the names below are informational only.

**Results:** resolves on the results certified by the Georgia Secretary of State. It may resolve earlier once the Associated Press has called the race and no recount, contest or runoff that could change the winner remains pending. If a recount or court-ordered correction changes the certified winner before resolution, the corrected certified result controls.

**Postponement or cancellation:** if the general election is postponed, the market stays open until the rescheduled election for the same term. If no election for this office and term is held, it resolves N/A.

payload.descriptionMarkdown:
This market resolves to the **party** of the winner of the 2026 election for **U.S. Representative for Illinois's 10th congressional district** — the term beginning January 3, 2027.

**Which round counts:** the November 3, 2026 general election (plurality winner). Primaries do not count.

**Party rule:** the winner's party is the party **on whose line or with whose party designation they appear on the official general-election ballot**. A candidate nominated by Democratic Party or Republican Party who also appears on other parties' lines (fusion) counts as that party's candidate. Candidates who are independent, have no party preference, or belong to any other party resolve to "Another party or independent", even if they say they would caucus with a major party. Later party switches, caucus decisions, resignations or deaths after the result is certified do **not** change the resolution.

**Replacements:** if a nominee withdraws, dies or is replaced before the election, the market still resolves to the party of the certified winner; the names below are informational only.

**Results:** resolves on the state's certified results. It may resolve earlier once the Associated Press has called the race and no recount, contest or runoff that could change the winner remains pending. If a recount or court-ordered correction changes the certified winner before resolution, the corrected certified result controls.

**Postponement or cancellation:** if the general election is postponed, the market stays open until the rescheduled election for the same term. If no election for this office and term is held, it resolves N/A.

- Carl Lambrecht — Republican
- Brad Schneider — Democratic

seed.basis: SEED, not a forecast: Cook PVI D+12, incumbent-party bonus D+3, neutral national environment, logistic scale 4 pts → P(D|two-party)=98%, clamped to 3–97%; 2% reserved for another party/independent/write-in.

**Party rule:** the winner's party is the party **on whose line or with whose party designation they appear on the official general-election ballot**. A candidate nominated by Democratic Party or Republican Party who also appears on other parties' lines (fusion) counts as that party's candidate. Candidates who are independent, have no party preference, or belong to any other party resolve to "Another party or independent", even if they say they would caucus with a major party. Later party switches, caucus decisions, resignations or deaths after the result is certified do **not** change the resolution.

**Replacements:** if a nominee withdraws, dies or is replaced before the election, the market still resolves to the party of the certified winner; the names below are informational only.

**Results:** resolves on the state's certified results. If a recount or court-ordered correction changes the certified winner before resolution, the corrected certified result controls.
